title: Simple maps pull back inner-anodyne maps to labelled inner-anodyne maps
statement:
Use small monoidal infinity categories, $C_\otimes$, labelled representables and space-valued presheaves from [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. Let $p:C_\otimes\to\Delta$ be the structural cartesian fibration, and let $p^*$ denote presheaf restriction and $p_!$ its left Kan extension adjoint. In $P(\Delta)$ let $\mathcal A_\Delta$ be the smallest class containing the discrete inner horn inclusions $\Lambda^a_b\to\Delta^a$, $a\geq2$, $0<b<a$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. In $P(C_\otimes)$ let $\mathcal A_C$ be the corresponding class generated by
$$\Delta^a(\boldsymbol e)\times_{p^*\Delta^a}p^*\Lambda^a_b\longrightarrow\Delta^a(\boldsymbol e),\qquad \boldsymbol e\in C^a.$$
Let $L\in P(\Delta)$ and $f:X\to p^*L$ be a map. Call $f$ simple if, for every $\sigma:\Delta^a\to L$ (all $a\geq0$), the pullback $X_\sigma=X\times_{p^*L}p^*\Delta^a$ is representable and the adjoint of its projection, $p_!X_\sigma\to\Delta^a$, is an equivalence. Thus it is the projection, not just the underlying object, which must identify with a represented labelled simplex over $\Delta^a$. If $f$ is simple and $u:K\to L$ lies in $\mathcal A_\Delta$, then
$$X\times_{p^*L}p^*K\longrightarrow X$$
lies in $\mathcal A_C$.

source.place: Definition 6.7 and Proposition 6.9 (which invokes Chu–Haugseng, Enriched infinity-operads, Lemma 2.7.14 (arXiv:1707.08049; Haugseng bibliography [1])); read online. No Stacks tag covers labelled infinity-categorical inner-anodyne maps.

proof.text:
Work in the fixed small universe of the presheaf definitions. For a presheaf $T$ equipped with a map $t:T\to L$, put $\Phi(T,t)=X\times_{p^*L}p^*T$, with its projection to $X$; maps over $L$ give maps over $X$. The cited free-cocompletion result supplies small presheaf colimits, and the cited pointwise theorem computes these colimits and pullbacks objectwise. A colimit of objects over a fixed base is their underlying colimit equipped with its induced map to that base: this follows from the colimit universal property by taking the homotopy fibers imposing compatibility with the base. At $c\in C_\otimes$, restriction gives $(p^*T)(c)=T(p(c))$, so restriction preserves those colimits. The space-valued pullback comparison in the cited universality theorem, applied over the small space $L(p(c))$ along $X(c)\to L(p(c))$, therefore gives
$$\operatorname{colim}_j\Phi(T_j,t_j)(c)\simeq X(c)\times_{L(p(c))}\operatorname{colim}_jT_j(p(c))\simeq\Phi(\operatorname{colim}_jT_j,t)(c).$$
The comparisons are natural. The componentwise-equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] then makes this a presheaf equivalence over $X$. Consequently $\Phi:P(\Delta)_{/L}\to P(C_\otimes)_{/X}$ preserves all small colimits, in particular pushouts and ordinal colimits. Here slices mean maps to the displayed base and coherently commuting triangles; no strict fiber product is substituted for a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Lemma 2.7.14 proof, colimit preservation and base-change reduction, expanded using objectwise presheaf calculations; Proposition 2.7.8, universality argument.

proof.text:
Let $\sigma:\Delta^a\to L$. Simplicity says that $X_\sigma$ is represented by an object $e=[r](\boldsymbol e)$ of $C_\otimes$ and that the adjoint $p_!X_\sigma\to\Delta^a$ of its projection is an equivalence. Yoneda evaluation and the defining adjunction give, naturally in $G\in P(\Delta)$,
$$\operatorname{Map}(p_!y(e),G)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(y(e),p^*G)\simeq G([r])\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\Delta^r,G).$$
By Yoneda full faithfulness (applied also to the opposite presheaf category in a containing universe), this identifies $p_!y(e)$ with $\Delta^r$. Under this identification the adjoint projection is induced by a monotone map $\alpha:[r]\to[a]$. Yoneda full faithfulness makes $\alpha$ an isomorphism because its represented map is an equivalence. An order isomorphism of finite ordinals forces $r=a$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. The labels of $e$ thus form a list in $C^a$. Under the adjunction its identity base map corresponds precisely to the structural unit $y(e)\to p^*\Delta^a$. Thus $X_\sigma\to p^*\Delta^a$ is equivalent OVER $p^*\Delta^a$ to $\Delta^a(\boldsymbol e)\to p^*\Delta^a$, not merely equivalent as an underlying presheaf.

source.place: Definition 2.7.11 and Lemma 2.7.14, identification of the pulled-back representable and its adjoint projection; Haugseng arXiv:2311.13362v1 Definition 6.7.

proof.text:
For an inner horn $h:\Lambda^a_b\to\Delta^a$ and any $\sigma:\Delta^a\to L$, associating the homotopy pullbacks gives
$$\Phi(\Lambda^a_b,\sigma h)\simeq X_\sigma\times_{p^*\Delta^a}p^*\Lambda^a_b,$$
compatibly with the arrow to $\Phi(\Delta^a,\sigma)=X_\sigma$. Step 2 identifies this arrow with the labelled inner horn generator
$$\Delta^a(\boldsymbol e)\times_{p^*\Delta^a}p^*\Lambda^a_b\longrightarrow\Delta^a(\boldsymbol e).$$
It therefore belongs to $\mathcal A_C$. This calculation only uses the defining pullback and the over-base identification; it does not assume that arbitrary pullbacks preserve inner anodyne maps.

source.place: Lemma 2.7.14, final two pullback squares and generator identification; Haugseng Proposition 6.9 applied to the horn generators.

proof.text:
Define a class $\mathcal W$ of arrows $v:A\to B$ in $P(\Delta)$ by requiring that, for EVERY $t:B\to L$, the arrow $\Phi(A,tv)\to\Phi(B,t)$ belongs to $\mathcal A_C$. By step 3 every ordinary inner horn inclusion belongs to $\mathcal W$. To verify pushout closure, let $v\in\mathcal W$, form $B'=B\amalg_A A'$, and fix any $t':B'\to L$. Restricting $t'$ equips the entire pushout diagram with maps to $L$. Step 1 sends this pushout to
$$\Phi(B',t')\simeq\Phi(B,t'|_B)\amalg_{\Phi(A,t'|_A)}\Phi(A',t'|_{A'}).$$
The arrow $\Phi(A',t'|_{A'})\to\Phi(B',t')$ is a pushout of the image of $v$, which is in $\mathcal A_C$ by the definition of $\mathcal W$. It belongs to $\mathcal A_C$ by its defining pushout closure. Since $t'$ was arbitrary, $A'\to B'$ belongs to $\mathcal W$.

source.place: Proposition 2.7.8, closure under cobase change; Lemma 2.7.14 proof. The class with all maps of the codomain to L makes the slice argument explicit.

proof.text:
For transfinite closure, let $(A_\beta)_{\beta\leq\lambda}$ be a small continuous ordinal diagram whose successor arrows are in $\mathcal W$, and fix $t:A_\lambda\to L$. Put $t_\beta=t\circ(A_\beta\to A_\lambda)$. At every successor stage the arrow $\Phi(A_\beta,t_\beta)\to\Phi(A_{\beta+1},t_{\beta+1})$ lies in $\mathcal A_C$, since $t_{\beta+1}$ is one of the maps tested in the definition of $\mathcal W$. At each limit ordinal $\gamma\leq\lambda$, step 1 identifies
$$\Phi(A_\gamma,t_\gamma)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\gamma}\Phi(A_\beta,t_\beta).$$
Thus the image is itself a continuous transfinite composition of arrows of $\mathcal A_C$. Its composite is in $\mathcal A_C$ by the defining closure of that class. As this holds for every $t$, the composite $A_0\to A_\lambda$ is in $\mathcal W$. The zero-length case is an identity, as included in transfinite-composition closure; no large ordinal or colimit outside the fixed universe is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.7.8, closure under transfinite compositions, with the continuous diagram and its limit stages written out.

proof.text: For retract closure, suppose $v:A\to B$ is a retract of $w:A'\to B'$ in the arrow category, with codomain maps $i_B:B\to B'$ and $r_B:B'\to B$ satisfying $r_Bi_B=\mathrm{id}_B$ (with the coherent retract data). If $w\in\mathcal W$ and $t:B\to L$, equip $B'$ with $tr_B$ and each domain with the composite through its arrow. The retract diagram is now over $L$: on $B$, $tr_Bi_B=t$, and on domains the same equality follows from the commuting arrow squares. Applying the functor $\Phi$ preserves the retract data. The image of $w$ is in $\mathcal A_C$, so its retract, the image of $v$, is in $\mathcal A_C$. Hence $\mathcal W$ is retract closed. Steps 3--5 and this retract calculation show that $\mathcal W$ is weakly saturated and contains all the inner horns. By the defining minimality of $\mathcal A_\Delta$, it contains $\mathcal A_\Delta$. Apply this to $u:K\to L$ and the tested map $\mathrm{id}_L$: since $\Phi(L,\mathrm{id}_L)\simeq X$, the resulting arrow is exactly $X\times_{p^*L}p^*K\to X$, proving the claim.

source.place: Proposition 2.7.8, retract closure, and Lemma 2.7.14; Haugseng Definition 6.1 and Proposition 6.9. Expanded without invoking a small-object factorization.
